messages:
Alex W: Ran a 30m soak in staging with synthetic traffic to validate per-key bursts + circuit-breaker fallback. Saw unexpected 503s when we hit ~3x burst tokens even though per-org quota had headroom. Sharing quick logs and timings below.

deploy-bot: loadtest-run finished: total=210k reqs, errors=2.4% (mostly 503), 95p latency=210ms, job=staging-burst-fuzz-2026-03-17

Priya S: which enforcement policy did you test against? per-org or per-key? and are we using the new cb (circuit-breaker) wrapper from last week?

Alex W: per-key primarily, with per-org as fallback. policy snippet we used:
```json
{"type":"leaky_bucket","rate":120,"burst":300,"cb":{"threshold_pct":0.25,"min_requests":20,"window_ms":10000}}
```

Jamal K: curious — cb.threshold_pct=0.25 seems aggressive for bursty workloads. 503s often line up with cache misses on prefixes (KV cache warmup). did you correlate with kv-cache.hit_rate?

Alex W: I pulled kv traces; hit_rate dipped from 0.92 -> 0.55 during the spikes. 503 spikes align with cb.open events in control-plane logs.

Sasha L: can you paste a short timeline? like minute-by-minute bucket fill + cb state?

Alex W: first 10m steady, small bursts tolerated. at 12:34 UTC a sustained spike (5s bursts every 10s) pushed some keys to burst>burst_limit and cb flipped open for ~15s per key, causing 503s.

Maddy Ops: heads-up — there was a control-plane config rollout at 12:33 (rolled back 12:36) that touched quota-cache invalidation. might be related :grimacing: 

Alex W: reran the same test with control-plane pinned to previous revision (no rollout) and saw same pattern, so not entirely rollout-related.

Priya S: two ideas: (1) emit enforcement_layer in reject telemetry (per_key | per_org | cb_open), (2) add token-level trace_id to link requests -> bucket state in grafana traces. dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/staging/rate-limits (for reference).

Jamal K: agree. Also recommend we treat cb thresholds as function of fill_rate instead of absolute percent. For example, if fill_rate > X over Yms then open. That would avoid opening on brief spikes.

Sasha L: +1. Also can we add a small hysteresis so cb doesn't flip open/closed rapidly for the same key? maybe backoff windows per-key.

Maddy Ops: can console show a breakdown on the reject reason? customers keep asking whether the reject was per-key burst vs org-limit vs cb. If we have a short "reason" field we can surface it in the UI.

Alex W: we currently emit reject.code=RATE_EXCEEDED and cb.marker=CB_OPEN separately. I propose adding enforcement_layer: "per_key|per_org|cb" and reject_reason: "burst|sustained|cb_open" so Console can show it without heuristics.

Priya S: I'll add enforcement_layer and reject_reason to telemetry schema. Can we also have a staging-only "simulate" toggle in Console to apply a policy change without a full deploy? would speed iteration.

Jamal K: for next runs I can provide two fuzzers: (A) small frequent micro-bursts (200rps for 2s every 10s) and (B) slow ramp to saturation over 5m. script snippet for (A):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer STAGING_KEY" https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate & done; sleep 2; done
```

Sasha L: also test skewed traffic (1% of keys get 80% of traffic) — that's where per-key logic matters.

Maddy Ops: I'll open a quick runbook / rollout checklist to add the UI field and telemetry changes. we should also add an alert when cb.open_count > 10 in 1m in staging so SRE gets paged during tests.

incident-bot: created incident ticket PLAT-432: "staging rate-limit + cb validation" assigned to @Alex W and @Priya S

Alex W: OK I'll run the two tests (micro-burst + ramp + skew) tonight with token-level tracing enabled, upload logs, and paste a condensed timeline here. thanks all :thumbsup:
